title: A Millimeter Methanol Maser Ring Tracing the Deceleration of the Heat Wave Powered by the Massive Protostellar Accretion Outburst in G358.93─0.03 MM1
question: How do the millimeter CH3OH maser rings excited during the accretion outburst in G358.93-0.03 MM1 evolve in size and intensity over time to trace the propagation and deceleration of the outburst-driven heat wave?

data.sensitivity: 1.3 to 251 mJy beam^-1 per channel for ALMA cubes; 85 to 900 mJy beam^-1 for SMA cubes

what.value: 6.668 GHz (vt=0) CH3OH maser spot positions across 5 VLBI epochs

evidence.quote: Two cm maser lines of $A$-type CH$_3$OH were observed within a few days of this image, 6.668 GHz ($v_{t}$=0) with VLBI (cite: Burns2023)
Also shown in Fig. 3b are measurements of the diameter of the distribution of 6.7 GHz maser spots fit to 5 epochs of VLBI images by (cite: Burns2023).

recipe.goal: Measure exponential decay timescales of the 199 and 217 GHz maser lines
recipe.method: Fit exponential decay curves to the peak intensities and integrated flux densities of the 199 and 217 GHz maser lines across epochs
assumptions: Exponential decay of maser intensity over time

recipe.goal: Fit circular rings to maser spots in the highest resolution ALMA cubes
recipe.method: Independently fit several maser spots around the ring in three high-resolution ALMA epochs (2019.451, 2019.538, 2019.552) and fit those positions with a circle accounting for position uncertainties
assumptions: Maser spots trace a circular ring
Distance of 6.75 kpc to convert angular diameter to au

recipe.goal: Perform 2-component Gaussian fitting on smoothed ALMA and SMA cubes and infer ring diameters
recipe.method: Smooth higher-resolution ALMA cubes to match lower-resolution epochs (SMA beam for 217 GHz; 2019.286 ALMA beam for 199 GHz epoch 2019.552), fit two fixed-beam Gaussians per channel using CASA imfit, filter fits by residual and R.A. separation criteria, and take the 90th percentile chord length as the ring diameter
key_parameters: Component size and position angle fixed to synthesized beamsize
Peak absolute intensity in 2-component fit residual < 0.4 times that of single-component fit
Integrated absolute flux in 2-component fit residual < 0.6 times that of single-component fit
Separation of fitted components in right ascension between 0.09'' and 0.40''
Diameter taken as 90th percentile of separations; uncertainty from 80th and 100th percentiles added in quadrature with theta / median SNR
assumptions: Ring-like structure was pervasive in time across epochs

recipe.goal: Fit power-law expansion model to maser ring diameters over time
recipe.method: Fit a fractional power law R = a(t - t0)^m to the inferred diameters from the 2-component fits of the millimeter maser images, and compare with 6.7 GHz VLBI maser spot diameters
key_parameters: 50000 Monte Carlo trial fits with bootstrap resampling
assumptions: R = 0 at t = t0 = 2019.0479 (maser flare inception)

answer_key.quantity: 199 GHz maser peak intensity e-folding decay time

evidence.quote: Both millimeter maser lines (199 and 217 GHz) decayed exponentially (Fig. 3a), with fitted $e$-folding times of 19.7$\pm$0.38 and 61.7$\pm$7.4 days, respectively, for their peak intensities, and 20.0$\pm$0.5 and 44.9$\pm$8.5 days for their integrated flux densities.

evidence.quote: Fitting the angular extent of the millimeter masers versus time yields a power law of index 0.39$\pm$0.06, which also reproduces the observed extent of the 6.7 GHz masers in the first VLBI epoch of (cite: Burns2020).

Fitting the inferred diameters from the 2-component fits to the millimeter maser images using a fractional power law, $R=a(t-t_0)^m$, assuming $R$=0 at $t$=$t_0$=2019.0479 corresponding to the maser flare inception (cite: Sugiyama19) yields $m$ = 0.39$\pm$0.06.

answer_key.quantity: Mean radial expansion velocity of millimeter maser ring

evidence.quote: the diameter of the ring increased by $\gtrsim$60% (from $\approx$1100 to $\approx$1800 au in the 217 GHz line) over 200 days, consistent with an average radial propagation rate of $\approx$0.01c, while the maser intensity declined exponentially.

Based on the millimeter maser data, the extent of the maser emission increased by $\gtrsim$60% ($\sim$1100 au to $\sim$1800 au in the 217 GHz line), corresponding to a mean radial expansion velocity of 0.01$c$.

score_reason: ALMA project codes, observing epochs, frequencies, channel widths, weighting schemes, beamsizes, and the step-by-step 2-component fitting and filtering criteria are clearly documented. However, reproducing the full time-series requires non-ALMA (SMA) cubes from Brogan et al. (2019), unstated initial spot coordinates per channel, and unstated self-calibration and tclean imaging parameters.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA data (2018.A.00031.T and 2019.1.00768.S) are public in the archive, the main scientific results are well-defined quantitative measurements (ring diameters across epochs, e-folding decay timescales, and the expansion power-law index m = 0.39 +/- 0.06), and the CASA imfit / scipy.odr methodology is specified with explicit quantitative acceptance criteria.
